oil.summary: Crude markets posted a split session Friday: Brent edged up 0.50% to $94.25/bbl while WTI slipped 0.88% to $87.05, capping a strong weekly gain of roughly 6% for both benchmarks. The bullish weekly narrative is anchored by three supply-shock themes: the collapse of an Iran nuclear deal that has pushed Iranian exports to zero per reports, continued Strait of Hormuz restrictions, and Ukrainian drone strikes on Lukoil's Perm-region refinery and the Taneco/Tamanneftegaz complex. On the softer side, the White House temporarily eased Russia sanctions to contain the price surge, a move that has irritated European allies. RBOB gasoline cratered 6.70% on the day and is down nearly 13% on the month, suggesting demand-side pressure at the pump. Saudi Arabia has rerouted Mediterranean exports via Sidi Kerir, up ~33%, to bypass Houthi threats, while Venezuela's export ceiling—due to port infrastructure failures—is keeping tankers waiting up to a month.
drivers: Iran deal collapse and Hormuz restrictions driving supply-risk premium; Iranian exports reported at zero
Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refining infrastructure (Lukoil Perm, Taneco) disrupting Russian downstream capacity
RBOB gasoline down 6.70% on the day, signaling demand weakness even as crude holds; US temporarily eases Russia sanctions to cap price surge

gas.summary: Henry Hub gained 2.49% on the day to $2.801/MMBtu, recovering modestly but still down nearly 4% on the month, keeping US gas in a soft medium-term trend. European TTF surged 1.67% to €66.385/MWh and is up over 8% on the week and more than 7% on the month, reflecting tighter continental balances likely linked to the broader Russia-Ukraine conflict dynamics and re-routing of energy flows discussed in oil markets. Headline flow specific to gas was thin today; Baker Hughes data showed the US oil-and-gas rig count fell this week despite rising crude prices, which could restrain associated gas output at the margin. No LNG-specific or storage data was available in today's feed.
drivers: TTF up 8% on the week, diverging sharply from Henry Hub, reflecting tighter European supply amid Russia-Ukraine conflict disruptions
US rig count declined week-on-week despite higher oil prices, potentially capping associated gas supply growth
Henry Hub monthly trend remains negative (-3.94%), limiting upside conviction on the US domestic gas trade

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs ticked up 1.21% to $78.50/EUA but are essentially flat on the week (+0.12%) and down 4% on the month, suggesting the market is not yet pricing the TTF gas surge fully into carbon abatement economics. TTF at €66.39/MWh—up over 8% on the week—raises the cost of gas-fired generation and could incrementally support carbon prices if coal-to-gas switching assumptions shift. On the renewables side, today's headlines focus on India: solar developers are adding battery storage to reduce large-scale curtailment, and a separate report highlights that India is building clean power faster than it can absorb. Headline flow for European power fundamentals was limited today beyond TTF price action.
drivers: TTF up 8% on the week raises gas-fired generation costs, creating potential upside pressure on EUAs if fuel-switching dynamics tighten
EU EUA flat on the week despite gas surge, suggesting the carbon market is not yet fully repricing generation economics
India scaling battery-storage additions to address solar curtailment—no direct EU power market impact but signals accelerating clean-energy integration globally
